working_title: No Cash Flows, New Owners: Spot Bitcoin ETFs and the Origins of Comovement
research_question: Did the January 2024 approval of US spot Bitcoin ETFs change the co-movement between Bitcoin returns and US equity returns?
note_on_scope: The work order named two deliverables (data_dictionary.json and a short data_plan.md). Pipeline output discipline permits exactly one artifact, so the data plan is embedded here as the `data_plan` object rather than written as a second file. Nothing from the requested plan has been dropped.

treatment.event_name: SEC approval and commencement of trading of eleven US spot Bitcoin ETPs
treatment.why_2024m2_not_2024m1: Donut specification from identification_strategy.md §7: 2023m8-2024m1 is excluded to absorb Grayscale-ruling anticipation, the two false-news events, listing week itself, and the GBTC redemption transition. The no-donut variant (treatment from 2024-01-11) is built in parallel as d_post_listing_raw.

sample.deviation_from_work_order: The work order anticipated '~3 years pre and ~1.5+ years post'. As of the 2026-09-11 extract the post-period is 31 months (2.6 years), exactly matching the 31-month clean pre-period. This symmetry is a gain, not a change of design, and should be stated in the paper's data section.

naming.style: snake_case throughout; no spaces, no capitals, no units in the value (units live in this dictionary)

prefixes.rx_: excess log return over the daily risk-free rate
prefixes.y_: estimation outcome (the LHS of a regression)

suffixes._ec: computed on the equity-close clock (16:00 ET to 16:00 ET) - the BASELINE
suffixes._utc: computed on the 00:00 UTC to 00:00 UTC clock - ROBUSTNESS

return_definition.functional_form: log (continuously compounded) returns: r_t = ln(P_t) - ln(P_{t-1})
return_definition.units: decimal per period. Multiply by 100 only at the reporting layer; never store percent in the panel.
return_definition.price_basis_equities: split- and dividend-adjusted close (yfinance default). px_close_raw retained alongside for the ETF premium/discount work, where the unadjusted print is the right object.
return_definition.price_basis_crypto: raw close. No adjustment concept applies.
return_definition.excess_returns: rx = r - rf, with rf the Ken French daily risk-free rate converted from percent to decimal. Applied to the equity market factor and, for the beta specifications, to the crypto leg as well.

timezone_alignment.why_this_section_exists: Crypto trades 24/7; US equities close at 16:00 ET. The clock choice is not a formatting detail - it changes the estimate. identification_strategy.md §2 identifies resynchronization as the single most underrated threat: if the ETF relocated Bitcoin price discovery into US cash hours, a daily correlation measured on a 16:00 ET clock rises MECHANICALLY even with an unchanged 24-hour covariance. The clock convention is therefore specified here, before any estimation, and a timing-invariant outcome (rho_3d_m, beta_dimson_m) is built alongside it.
timezone_alignment.master_clock: America/New_York (ET), DST-aware. Every timestamp is stored in the data files as tz-aware UTC; every join key is date_et, the NYSE session date derived from that UTC instant.
timezone_alignment.never_hardcode_offset: 16:00 ET is 21:00 UTC under EST and 20:00 UTC under EDT. Do the conversion with a tz database (zoneinfo / pytz 'America/New_York'), never with a fixed offset. A fixed -5 offset silently corrupts roughly 8 months of every year.

baseline_clock.name: equity_close_clock
baseline_clock.crypto_return_for_session_t: r_ec[i,t] = ln P_i(16:00 ET on session t) - ln P_i(16:00 ET on session t-1), where t-1 is the PREVIOUS NYSE SESSION, not the previous calendar day.
baseline_clock.equity_return_for_session_t: r_ec[mkt,t] = ln P_mkt(close, t) - ln P_mkt(close, t-1), the same session pair.
baseline_clock.why_this_is_exactly_synchronous: Because t-1 is the previous NYSE session for BOTH legs, the crypto and equity return windows span an identical wall-clock interval, including across weekends and holidays. Monday's crypto return is a Friday-16:00-to-Monday-16:00 three-day return, and Monday's equity return is a Friday-close-to-Monday-close three-day return. No non-synchronicity remains by construction. This is the property that the 00:00 UTC clock does not have.
baseline_clock.construction_from_hourly_bars: The 16:00 ET price is the close of the hourly bar whose RIGHT edge is 16:00 ET (i.e. the 15:00-16:00 ET bar). Provider bar labelling differs: yfinance labels 60m bars by their LEFT edge, so select the bar with ET hour == 15. A build-time assertion (see qa_checks.qa_04) verifies the convention against a day with a known large intraday move before the panel is accepted.
baseline_clock.availability_constraint: BLOCKING. See availability_audit.aud_03. Hourly crypto bars are the only way to strike a 16:00 ET price, and the only configured hourly source (yfinance 60m) is capped at the trailing 730 days, i.e. from roughly 2024-09-12 onward. The baseline clock is therefore NOT constructible over the pre-period with current credentials. Resolution paths are enumerated in data_plan.blockers.blk_01.

robustness_clock.name: utc_day_clock
robustness_clock.crypto_return_for_session_t: r_utc[i,t] = ln P_i(close of the UTC calendar day t) - ln P_i(close of UTC calendar day t-1). This is exactly the yfinance daily crypto bar dated t - verified, the bars are stamped 00:00:00+00:00.
robustness_clock.alignment_rule: Join the UTC-day return dated t to the NYSE session dated t. Sessions on which equities are closed are dropped from the daily estimation panel (retained in crypto_offday_returns for the weekend test F14).
robustness_clock.non_synchronicity_this_induces: The UTC crypto day for date t ends at 19:00 ET (EST) or 20:00 ET (EDT) - that is 3 to 4 hours AFTER the equity close - and begins 20 to 21 hours BEFORE it. The mismatch is two-sided, not a simple lead or lag, which is why a single Scholes-Williams lag correction is insufficient and the 3-day-return construction (rho_3d_m) is the preferred invariance check.
robustness_clock.status: AVAILABLE for the full 2021-01-01 to 2026-08-31 window, verified. With current credentials this clock is the only one that spans the sample, so it is the DE FACTO baseline until blk_01 is resolved. The paper must report which clock produced the headline number.

session_partition.defined_on: ET wall clock, so the boundaries track US market hours through DST transitions

sessions.note: Nested, not a partition element. Used only in the companion DDD specification of identification_strategy.md §6.4; never summed with the other four.

session_partition.dst_caveat: Anchoring sessions to the ET clock means the Asian session drifts by one hour in Tokyo local time across DST changes. That is the correct choice, because the treatment operates through a US-listed vehicle whose hours are ET-anchored. A robustness variant fixing 'asia' on the Tokyo local clock (09:00-17:00 JST) is specified as sens_04.
session_partition.equity_leg: S&P 500 E-mini future (CME ticker ES, front month, rolled on volume). ES trades 18:00-17:00 ET with a one-hour break, which is what makes the covariance well defined in the Asian and European sessions. STATUS: BLOCKED - no configured wrapper serves CME intraday. See blk_02.

calendar.trading_calendar: NYSE (XNYS) via pandas_market_calendars. Half-days (day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, July 3) close at 13:00 ET; on those sessions the equity-close clock strikes at 13:00 ET, not 16:00 ET, for both legs. A half_day flag is carried in the panel and a robustness variant drops them.
calendar.crypto_calendar: 365 days. Days on which the NYSE is closed are excluded from asset_panel_daily and written to crypto_offday_returns.
calendar.month_definition: Calendar month, ET. n_days_m is the count of NYSE sessions in the month with a non-missing return on both legs; cells with n_days_m < 15 are flagged and, per the pre-analysis plan, dropped from the headline with the kept-version reported in robustness.

missing_data.sentinel: null in JSON, NaN in parquet. Never 0, never -999.
missing_data.policy: No forward-filling of crypto prices. A missing hourly bar leaves the derived return missing; a gap longer than 3 hours inside a session voids that session-day cell for that asset. Exchange outages are logged in data_exceptions rather than patched.

outlier_policy.baseline: No winsorization in the headline specification.
outlier_policy.robustness: Winsorize returns at the 0.5 / 99.5 percentiles, computed within asset over the full sample. Reported both ways per paper_plan.md §6.

columns.description: rho_m^2. MUST be reported next to every correlation. At rho = 0.4 only 16 percent of Bitcoin's return variance is equity-driven; the magnitude discipline in paper_plan.md §11 forbids writing 'Bitcoin became a risk asset' on the strength of a correlation alone.

columns.name: beta_m
columns.description: Secondary outcome. See dv_09.

columns.name: ln_sigma_ratio_m
columns.description: ln(sigma_i / sigma_mkt). The F10 decomposition: beta = rho * sigma_ratio, so d(ln beta) = d(artanh-ish rho term) + d(ln sigma_ratio). Bitcoin's realized volatility fell over the sample, so a beta-based outcome mixes the object of interest with a volatility trend. This column is what separates them.

columns.name: rho_3d_m
columns.description: Correlation of non-overlapping 3-session returns within the month. TIMING-INVARIANT. The core of falsification F9: it cannot be moved by a shift in WHEN within the day information is impounded.

columns.name: beta_dimson_m
columns.description: Sum of the coefficients on the lead, contemporaneous and lagged market return. The Dimson/Scholes-Williams construction.

columns.name: rho_dcc_m
columns.description: DCC-GARCH conditional correlation averaged within the month. Alternative outcome, descriptive - a DCC correlation that rises in January 2024 is exactly as confounded as a rolling correlation that rises in January 2024.

columns.name: n_days_m
columns.description: Sessions with non-missing returns on both legs. Enters the Fisher-z variance 1/(n_m - 3) and the min-15 inclusion rule.

columns.name: se_fisherz
columns.description: sqrt(1/(n_days_m - 3)). Known analytically and - this is the point - the SAME for every coin and every month given n. The generated-outcome error is therefore classical, homoskedastic and mean-zero: it inflates standard errors but does not bias tau, and the inflation is analytically removable. The sampling variance of beta_m, by contrast, scales with sigma_i/sigma_mkt and differs by an order of magnitude between BTC and a small-cap altcoin, which would make the DiD residual variance itself a function of treatment status. This is why Fisher-z is the headline and beta is not.

columns.name: d_etf_listed
columns.description: THE TREATMENT. See dv_20.

columns.name: d_post_etf
columns.description: Time-only post indicator, for the fallback single-series specification

columns.name: d_donut
columns.description: 1 for 2023m8 through 2024m1. Dropped in the baseline; retained in the no-donut robustness.

columns.name: d_anticipation
columns.description: Same window, used as its own regime in the three-regime specification where the anticipation coefficient is itself interpretable

columns.name: event_k
columns.description: m - T_i, for the event-study specification. K = 24 leads and lags, binned at the endpoints, reference k = -1. null for never-treated coins.

columns.name: cohort
columns.description: treated_btc | eventually_treated | never_treated

columns.name: d_in_headline_sample
columns.description: BTC plus never-treated coins only. Eventually-treated coins are excluded so no already-treated unit ever serves as a comparison - which is why the negative-weights problem does not arise and TWFE is admissible here.

columns.name: mkt_proxy
columns.description: Which equity proxy produced this row: MKT | SPY | QQQ | IWM | ACWX. The panel is built long over proxies so F8 is a filter, not a rebuild.

datasets.name: coin_session_month_panel
datasets.source: derived from T02 (crypto hourly) + ES intraday (BLOCKED)
datasets.description: The session DDD panel (identification_strategy.md §6.4). The paper's strongest attribution test and the only design that removes BTC-specific time shocks, because the coin-month fixed effect absorbs the halving and the election outright.

columns.name: session_id
columns.description: asia | europe | us_cash | us_post

columns.name: y_fisherz_corr_session
columns.description: Fisher-z of the within-month correlation between the coin's session-s return and the ES session-s return

columns.name: rcov_session
columns.description: Realized covariance: sum over days in the month of r[i,s,d] * r[es,s,d]. The level object behind the F13 test Delta_Cov_US - Delta_Cov_Asia > 0.

columns.name: rvar_session_share
columns.description: Session share of the coin's daily return variance. The mechanism predicts the US-cash share rises post-2024 for BTC and not for controls.

columns.name: d_us_cash
columns.description: The DDD interaction partner: lambda is identified off d_etf_listed x d_us_cash

columns.name: d_nav_strike
columns.description: Companion specification only; the 15:45-16:00 ET window nested inside us_cash

datasets.name: crypto_offday_returns
datasets.description: Crypto returns on days the NYSE is closed. Excluded from the estimation panel; retained for the F14 weekend-margin test, which is an independent corroboration from a direction the DiD does not use: if the ETF's marginal holder now sets the price, Bitcoin's weekend share of volume and volatility should FALL post-2024 and weekend returns should become less informative for Monday pricing.

columns.name: offday_type
columns.description: saturday | sunday | us_holiday

columns.name: w_weekend_vol_share
columns.description: Weekend realized variance divided by total weekly realized variance, per asset-week

derived_variables.name: r_ec
derived_variables.formula: r_ec[i,t] = ln( P_i(16:00 ET, t) ) - ln( P_i(16:00 ET, t-1) ), t-1 = previous NYSE session
derived_variables.role: BASELINE daily return for every asset. Exactly synchronous across legs by construction (see conventions.timezone_alignment.baseline_clock).

derived_variables.name: r_utc
derived_variables.formula: r_utc[i,t] = ln( P_i(00:00 UTC, t+1) ) - ln( P_i(00:00 UTC, t) ), i.e. the log change of the yfinance daily close dated t
derived_variables.role: ROBUSTNESS clock, and the de facto baseline until blk_01 clears. Two-sided non-synchronicity of +3/4h and -20/21h against the equity window.

derived_variables.name: rx_ec / rx_utc
derived_variables.formula: rx = r - rf, rf from ff_factors_daily (converted to decimal)
derived_variables.note: On multi-day spans (weekends) rf is summed over the calendar days in the span, not applied once.

derived_variables.name: rho_60d
derived_variables.formula: Pearson correlation of r[i] and r_mkt over the trailing 60 NYSE sessions, BACKWARD-LOOKING ONLY
derived_variables.role: Figures F1 and F3 and one robustness row. NEVER the headline.
derived_variables.warning: Adjacent daily values share 59 of 60 observations, inducing a mechanical MA(59). Two consequences that are routinely mishandled: a true effect phases in LINEARLY over 60 days rather than jumping, so an event-study plot on this series shows a ramp regardless of the true dynamics; and daily pre-trend tests are near-uninterpretable because pre-period values within 60 days of the event are contaminated by post-period returns. A centered window would be worse still - it contaminates plus and minus 30 days around the event.

derived_variables.name: beta_60d
derived_variables.formula: OLS slope of rx[i] on rx_mkt over the trailing 60 NYSE sessions
derived_variables.role: Figure only; same MA(59) warning as dv_04

derived_variables.name: beta_tvp_kalman
derived_variables.formula: State-space model, rx[i,t] = alpha_t + beta_t * rx_mkt_t + e_t, with (alpha_t, beta_t) a random walk; Kalman-smoothed
derived_variables.role: The cleanest device for LOCATING a break because it imposes no window. Descriptive, never identification.

derived_variables.name: rho_m
derived_variables.formula: Pearson correlation of r[i,t] and r_mkt[t] over the n_m NYSE sessions in calendar month m. Non-overlapping blocks.

derived_variables.name: y_fisherz_corr_equity
derived_variables.formula: artanh(rho_m) = 0.5 * ln( (1 + rho_m) / (1 - rho_m) )
derived_variables.role: THE PRIMARY OUTCOME. Unbounded, approximately normal, and with variance 1/(n_m - 3) that is known and identical across coins - which is exactly what makes the generated-outcome problem tractable and what the randomization and bootstrap inference rely on.
derived_variables.guard: Undefined at |rho| = 1. Assert |rho_m| < 0.999 and flag any cell that trips it rather than clipping silently.

derived_variables.name: beta_m
derived_variables.formula: OLS slope of rx[i,t] on rx_mkt[t] within month m
derived_variables.role: Secondary outcome, reported beside the primary. beta = rho * sigma_i / sigma_mkt, so it confounds the co-movement change with the relative-volatility trend.

derived_variables.name: ln_sigma_ratio_m
derived_variables.formula: ln( sd(r[i,t] over m) / sd(r_mkt[t] over m) )
derived_variables.role: The second leg of the F10 decomposition. Bitcoin's daily volatility runs roughly 3-5x the market's, so beta is roughly 3-5 rho and a small correlation change produces a large beta change. Reporting the two legs separately is what stops the paper from overstating.

derived_variables.name: rho2_m
derived_variables.formula: rho_m ** 2
derived_variables.role: Magnitude discipline. Printed adjacent to every correlation in every table, per paper_plan.md §11.

derived_variables.name: rho_3d_m
derived_variables.formula: Correlation of non-overlapping 3-session cumulative log returns within a rolling quarter (a month yields only ~7 three-day blocks, so this variable is computed on a 63-session block and mapped to the month of its endpoint)
derived_variables.role: The timing-invariance test (F9). Aggregating to 3-session returns absorbs any shift in when within the day information is impounded, so if the effect survives here it is not pure resynchronization. If it does NOT survive, the paper reports that the ETF re-timed price discovery without changing 24-hour covariance - which is itself a real and reportable result, not a failure.

derived_variables.name: beta_dimson_m
derived_variables.formula: Sum of b_{-1} + b_0 + b_{+1} from rx[i,t] = a + b_{-1} rx_mkt[t+1] + b_0 rx_mkt[t] + b_{+1} rx_mkt[t-1] + e, estimated on a 63-session block

derived_variables.name: rho_dcc_m
derived_variables.formula: Engle (2002) DCC-GARCH(1,1) on the bivariate (r[i], r_mkt) system, conditional correlation averaged within month; ADCC asymmetric variant reported alongside

derived_variables.name: rcov_session
derived_variables.formula: rcov[i,s,m] = sum over days d in m of ( r[i,s,d] * r[ES,s,d] ), where r[.,s,d] is the log return from the session-s open to the session-s close on day d
derived_variables.role: The session DDD level object. The F13 required finding is Delta_rcov_US - Delta_rcov_Asia > 0: a macro regime shift raises global risk-asset correlation in ALL sessions, whereas only a mechanism operating through a US-listed vehicle relocates covariance into US exchange hours.

derived_variables.name: rvar_session_share
derived_variables.formula: sum_d r[i,s,d]^2 / sum_d sum_s' r[i,s',d]^2, within month

derived_variables.name: w_weekend_vol_share
derived_variables.formula: Weekend realized variance / total weekly realized variance, per asset-week, using r_utc daily returns
derived_variables.role: F14. Constructible from daily UTC data alone - it does NOT depend on hourly coverage, which makes it the one piece of D2's logic that survives blk_01.

derived_variables.name: r_altidx_ew
derived_variables.formula: r_ALTIDX_EW[t] = (1/N) * sum over constituents i of r[i,t], daily-rebalanced equal weight
derived_variables.constituent_selection_rule: The list is FROZEN as of 2020-12-31, before the sample opens, and never rebalanced. This is a deliberate choice against a 'top-N by market cap' rule: selecting today's top N and running it backward would load the index with survivors and with coins that rose during the sample, which is precisely the look-ahead bias that manufactures spurious correlation dynamics. The frozen list is stated in the paper and the index is reported with and without ETH (which is eventually treated).
derived_variables.cap_weighted_variant: OPTIONAL and currently BLOCKED - historical market caps require CoinGecko or CoinMetrics, neither of which is configured. Do not approximate caps from price alone; supply changes over the sample.
derived_variables.role_restriction: Descriptive benchmark and synthetic-control donor. NOT a DiD control unit - it is a composite of units already in the panel and would double-count them.

derived_variables.name: flow_alloc / flow_basis
derived_variables.formula: Project daily aggregate net flow on the annualized CME futures basis, the change in CME open interest, and COT positioning: Flow_t = g0 + g1*Basis_t + g2*dOI_t + e_t. Fitted value = basis-trade flow; residual = allocation flow.
derived_variables.role: The H3 decomposition. H1 predicts the conditional beta loads on allocation flow (delta_A > 0) and not on basis flow (delta_B ~ 0). Validated against 13F filings of spot-ETF holders classified into hedge funds (basis traders), RIAs and wealth platforms (allocators), and other.
derived_variables.status: BLOCKED - requires T05 (flows, blocked) and CME futures basis/OI/COT (no configured source)

derived_variables.name: d_etf_listed
derived_variables.formula: d_etf_listed[i,m] = 1{ i == BTC } * 1{ m >= 2024m2 } in the headline sample; 1{ m >= T_i } with cohort-specific T_i in the staggered extension

variants.d_post_listing_raw: 1{ m >= 2024m1 }, no donut - the robustness variant
variants.d_post_etf: 1{ m >= 2024m2 } with no coin interaction - time-only, for the fallback single-series specification, which is descriptive and must be labelled as such in every table that reports it
variants.d_anticipation: 1{ 2023m8 <= m <= 2024m1 } - the middle regime in the three-regime specification

derived_variables.date_integrity_warning: SOL and XRP listing dates are null in asset_reference pending primary-source verification. The staggered extension MUST NOT be run until they are filled. A guessed cohort date does not fail loudly; it quietly biases the pooled ATT.

derived_variables.name: event_k
derived_variables.formula: event_k[i,m] = (months between m and T_i), binned at -24 and +24, reference k = -1
derived_variables.role: Event-study specification (identification_strategy.md §6.3). Joint F-test on k = -24..-2 is the pre-trend test; the Rambachan-Roth breakdown value Mbar is what the text should quote, not the pre-trend p-value - failing to reject a pre-trend with 31 monthly pre-observations is weak evidence.

qa_checks.check: Every date_et in asset_panel_daily is an XNYS trading session, and every XNYS session in the window appears. Symmetric difference must be empty.

For every crypto asset, r_ec and r_utc have correlation above 0.95 over the overlapping window (from 2024-09-12). A lower value means the hourly bar selection is mislabelled, not that the clocks genuinely disagree.
ff_factors_daily joins onto the session calendar with zero unmatched dates on either side over the common window. Do not left-join and coalesce - an unmatched date is a calendar bug.

Hourly bar-edge convention. Pick a session with a large, precisely timed intraday move and confirm that the bar selected as '16:00 ET close' contains the pre-16:00 price, not the post-16:00 one. Assert before any _ec column is written.
qa_checks.why: A one-bar labelling error shifts the entire baseline clock by an hour and would silently change the headline estimate.

qa_checks.check: x_dgs10 lies in (0, 20). If not, the ^TNX 10x scale convention applies - divide and re-assert.
|rho_m| < 0.999 for every cell, so artanh is finite. Flag, do not clip.
n_days_m >= 15 for every retained coin-month; the count of dropped cells is reported in the data appendix.
d_listed in etf_market_daily is 0 for every date before listing_date, and no zero-padded flow or volume rows exist pre-listing.
qa_checks.why: Zero-padding pre-listing manufactures a mechanical jump at 2024-01-11 in any aggregate.

qa_checks.check: DST transition days. On the two changeover Sundays each year, confirm the ET session partition still sums to 24 hours and that no bar is double-counted or dropped.
Every coin-month cell of the headline sample has cohort in {treated_btc, never_treated}. No eventually-treated unit may appear.
Cross-source price sanity: BTC close from yfinance versus at least one independent reference on ten randomly chosen days, agreeing within 0.5 percent.
qa_checks.note: This is the residue of the cross-venue validation paper_plan.md §6 asked for. With Allium unconfigured it cannot be done systematically.

qa_checks.check: No forward-fill anywhere in the price tables. Assert that no two consecutive rows of any crypto price series are bit-identical.

data_plan.one_paragraph_summary: The panel is a coin-month dataset of 13 crypto assets over 2021m1-2026m8 (68 months, roughly 884 cells), whose outcome is the Fisher-z of the within-month correlation between each coin's daily return and the US equity market return, with Bitcoin treated from 2024m2 and never-ETF'd coins as controls. Around it sit a daily asset panel, a session panel for the triple-difference, an ETF market and flow panel, and the macro and factor series. Everything on the equity side is verified available through the yfinance wrapper and the Ken French library. Two things are not: hourly crypto history before roughly 2024-09-12, which the 16:00 ET baseline clock and the session decomposition both require; and ETF net flows, which no configured wrapper serves. Those two gaps are not cosmetic - they bind on the paper's baseline clock and on two of its four designs - and they are stated as explicit asks below rather than papered over with proxies.

build_order.what: Pull daily prices for 13 crypto assets, 9 equity/commodity tickers, 11 ETF tickers and 3 macro indices via e2er-data yfinance history, every call with --save-to. Window 2020-12-01 to 2026-09-11 (the extra month gives a clean first return in January 2021).
Download the Ken French 5-factor daily and momentum daily files; divide by 100; join on date.
Assemble macro_daily from the yfinance fallback tickers; run the ^TNX scale assertion.
Build the NYSE session spine, compute r_utc for every asset, join the factors, apply qa_01 and qa_03.

Aggregate to non-overlapping calendar months: rho_m, Fisher-z, beta_m, ln_sigma_ratio_m, rho2_m, n_days_m, se_fisherz. Attach treatment, cohort, donut and event_k. Build the panel long over market proxies so F8 is a filter.

Pull 60m crypto and SPY bars for the trailing 730 days; run qa_04; build the post-period-only session panel.
build_order.status: partial - post-period only, which is not enough for a DDD

Ingest ETF daily flows and GBTC NAV inputs; build the aggregate flow series and the premium series.

cleaning_decisions_to_document_in_the_pa: Venue: single-source (Yahoo aggregated) crypto prices, not a cross-venue composite. The cross-venue validation the plan called for is reduced to the spot check in qa_11 because Allium is unconfigured. State this rather than implying a validation that was not performed.
Denomination: USD pairs throughout. The USD-versus-USDT question is not testable with this source; note it as a limitation.
Exchange outages and gaps: logged, never patched. A gap voids the affected cell.
Winsorization: none in the headline, 0.5/99.5 as robustness, both from a single build via d_winsor_flag.
US market holidays: crypto trades, equities do not. Excluded from the daily estimation panel, retained in T12 for F14.
Half-days: the equity-close clock strikes at 13:00 ET on NYSE half-days for both legs; flagged and available as a robustness exclusion.
Pre-listing ETF rows: absent, not zero. Zero-padding would manufacture a jump at 2024-01-11.
Index constituents: frozen as of 2020-12-31, never rebalanced, to avoid look-ahead in the altcoin index.

blockers.severity: HIGH - affects the declared baseline clock and the paper's strongest design
blockers.what: Hourly crypto (and intraday equity) history before roughly 2024-09-12 is unavailable. yfinance caps 60m data at the trailing 730 days; Allium is unconfigured.
blocks: the entire session decomposition D2 and the session DDD (T11, dv_15, dv_16, F13)
blockers.what_still_works: The full coin-month estimation panel on the UTC clock (T10), the event studies, the break tests, the synthetic control, and the weekend margin test F14 - which recovers part of D2's logic from daily data alone.
resolution_options: Set ALLIUM_API_KEY. Allium serves CEX trade data and would cover the crypto leg back to 2021, though not the CME equity leg.
CryptoCompare or Binance public klines REST - free, hourly OHLCV back to 2017, no key needed for Binance klines. Cheapest fix for the crypto leg.
CoinMetrics community reference rate at hourly frequency - the source paper_plan.md §6 names first, and the one with the best provenance story for a published paper.
For the equity leg: CME ES intraday via a data vendor, or Databento / Polygon.io. No free path.
blockers.interim_position: Report the headline on the UTC clock, state plainly that it is the robustness clock elevated to baseline by data availability, and hold the session DDD for the revision. Do NOT present a post-period-only session panel as a difference-in-differences - without a pre-period there is nothing to difference.

blockers.what: No configured source for CME E-mini S&P (ES) intraday prices.
blocks: the equity leg of every session-level covariance
blockers.why_spy_is_not_a_substitute: SPY trades 09:30-16:00 ET (plus thin extended hours). It cannot price the Asian or European sessions, which is exactly where the DDD's identifying contrast lives. Substituting SPY would make the US-cash session the only one with a defined covariance and would turn the triple-difference into a tautology.

blockers.severity: MEDIUM - blocks one of four designs
blockers.what: ETF daily net flows, shares outstanding, NAV and BTC holdings are unavailable from any configured wrapper. yfinance serves prices and volume only.
blockers.what_must_not_be_done: dollar_volume_usd (price x volume) is a gross turnover proxy and is NOT net flow. A day of heavy two-sided trading with zero net creation produces a large value. Using it in the dose-response would answer a different question while appearing to answer this one.
resolution_options: Farside Investors publishes the daily fund-by-fund flow table free; it is the de facto standard series in this literature.
Issuer daily disclosure pages (BlackRock, Fidelity, Bitwise, Grayscale) give shares outstanding, NAV and coins held - the primary-source version, and the one to prefer for a published paper.
Bloomberg, if terminal access exists, to cross-check both.
blockers.additional_gap: The CME futures basis, open interest and COT positioning that dv_19 projects flows onto also have no configured source. CME publishes COT and settlement data publicly; this is a scripting task, not an access problem.

blocks: the 10y TIPS real yield and the 10y breakeven
blockers.mitigated: VIX, MOVE, DXY and the 10y nominal all have verified yfinance substitutes. The headline specification takes no controls, so this does not touch the main estimate - it costs two rows in the descriptive table. A free key takes about thirty seconds to obtain.

blockers.what: SOL and XRP US spot ETF listing dates are unverified and are stored as null.
blocks: the staggered multi-cohort extension (Callaway-Sant'Anna, Sun-Abraham, Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess)
blockers.why_it_is_left_null: A guessed cohort date does not fail loudly. It quietly mis-assigns treatment timing and biases the pooled ATT, and no diagnostic in the pipeline would catch it. The dates must come from each fund's Form 8-A and the exchange listing notice.
blockers.does_not_block: The headline DiD, which uses BTC plus never-treated coins only and never touches these dates.

known_measurement_risks_carried_into_est: Resynchronization. If the ETF relocated price discovery into US hours, an equity-close-clock correlation rises mechanically. dv_12 (rho_3d_m) and dv_13 (beta_dimson_m) are the invariance checks, and the pre-committed reading if the effect vanishes under them is that the ETF re-timed price discovery without changing 24-hour covariance - a real result, reported as such.

Beta versus correlation. beta = rho * sigma_ratio and Bitcoin's volatility fell over the sample, so a beta outcome mixes the object of interest with a volatility trend. The panel carries both legs separately (dv_08, dv_10) so the decomposition is a filter, not a rebuild.
Generated outcome. The LHS is estimated. Fisher-z makes its variance known and coin-invariant, which keeps the error classical; se_fisherz is stored per cell so the two-step correction is available.

Rolling-window overlap. The 60-day series (dv_04, dv_05) are figure-only. The estimation panel is non-overlapping monthly blocks. This keeps the effective sample honest at roughly 68 months x 13 coins rather than 15,000 quasi-independent days.

One treated unit. Not a data issue, but it determines what the panel must support: the placebo grid needs every coin x every candidate month, so T10 is built over the full asset set and full window with no pre-filtering on treatment status.

handoff_to_econometrics.weights: none in the headline; 1/se_fisherz^2 as a robustness row (it is a legitimate GLS weight here precisely because se_fisherz is known)
handoff_to_econometrics.caveat_to_carry_forward: Until blk_01 is resolved, y_fisherz_corr_equity is computed on the 00:00 UTC clock, not the 16:00 ET clock the design declared as baseline. Every table must say which clock produced it.
